newsitem.title: USA: Exxon first quarter higher across board.
newsitem.headline: Exxon first quarter higher across board.

text.p: Exxon Corp's net income per share rose in the first quarter of 1997 to $0.87 from $0.76 a year ago as earnings at the oil giant rose to a quarterly record.
Net income rose 15 percent to $2.2 billion from $1.9 billion and improved in all business sectors, chairman Lee Raymond said in a statement released with the earnings figures.
Revenues were $33.6 billion against $31.2 billion a year ago.
Analysts had been looking for net income per share of $0.83 for the first quarter, according to investment network First Call.

U.S. exploration and production earnings rose to $554 million from $419 million, despite lower production volumes, while overseas earnings were $890 million compared with $1.0 billion, which includes a one-time credit of $125 million.

"Exploration and production earnings benefited from crude prices that were on average $3.00 higher than a year ago. However, by the end of the quarter crude oil had weakened, falling back to the levels of the year ago period," Exxon said.

Exxon's production volume was slightly lower at 1.6 million barrels per day (bpd) of liquids, compared with 1.7 million bpd a year ago, due to lower domestic output and the effects of a revised production sharing agreement with Malaysia.
U.S. refining and marketing turned round to a $57 million gain from a $16 million loss in the year ago and overseas refining and marketing income rose to $297 million from $190 million a year ago.

"Refinery throughput also rose over the prior year's quarter, despite higher scheduled maintenance activity. Industry refining margins were up from the very weak first quarter of 1996 as a result of declining supply costs," Exxon said.
Domestic chemicals earnings were stronger, up to $192 million from $153 million, while overseas operations slipped to $118 million from $134 million.
Worldwide, chemical earnings rose to $310 million from $287 million as sales rose five percent to 4.1 million tonnes.

"Although margins rose over the course of the quarter, they were on average similar to 1996's first quarter as higher product prices were offset by higher feedstock costs and unfavourable foreign exchange effects," the company said.

Earnings at the coal, minerals and power division rose to $128 million from $117 million and the company said that corporate finance expenses fell to $61 million from $116 million a year ago as a result of lower interest and tax-related expenses. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
